CodeContent:
# Profile Management & Dynamic Weather Updates

This plan outlines the implementation of a new Profile section that allows users to edit their personal information and farm details. Changing the farm location will dynamically update the coordinates, meaning the weather widget on the dashboard will accurately reflect the new location's real-time weather.

## Open Questions
- None. The approach uses Open-Meteo's geocoding to automatically resolve the user's typed address into precise coordinates before saving to the database.

## Proposed Changes

### Backend: API Endpoints

#### [MODIFY] `apps/backend/src/controllers/farm.controller.ts`
- Add an `updateMyFarm` controller method.
- This will allow the user to update their farm's `name`, `size`, `certification`, and `location` (address, latitude, longitude).

#### [MODIFY] `apps/backend/src/routes/farm.routes.ts`
- Add `router.put('/my-farm', authorize('FARMER'), updateMyFarm);`

#### [MODIFY] `apps/backend/src/controllers/auth.controller.ts`
- Add an `updateProfile` controller method to allow users to update their `firstName`, `lastName`, and `phone`.

#### [MODIFY] `apps/backend/src/routes/auth.routes.ts`
- Add `router.put('/me', authenticate, updateProfile);`

---

### Frontend: UI & Services

#### [MODIFY] `apps/web/src/services/farmService.ts`
- Add `updateMyFarm(data)` function to make the API call.

#### [MODIFY] `apps/web/src/services/authService.ts`
- Add `updateProfile(data)` function to make the API call.

#### [NEW] `apps/web/src/pages/Profile.tsx`
- Create a beautiful, responsive Profile settings page.
- Forms for editing Personal Details and Farm Details.
- Auto-geocoding: When the user enters a new address (e.g., "Delhi, India"), the frontend will automatically use Open-Meteo's geocoding API to resolve the precise latitude and longitude and save it alongside the address.

#### [MODIFY] `apps/web/src/App.tsx`
- Add the `/profile` route to the application.

#### [MODIFY] `apps/web/src/pages/FarmerDashboardNew.tsx`
- Update the dashboard's "MacDock" navigation to include a "Profile" icon linking to `/profile`.

## Verification Plan

### Manual Verification
1. Click the "Profile" icon in the navigation dock.
2. Change the Farm's location to a completely different city (e.g., from "Bengaluru" to "London, UK").
3. Save the profile.
4. Navigate back to the Dashboard.
5. Verify that the weather widget accurately displays the real-time weather for London!

CodeContent:
# Feature Update: Profile Management & Real-Time Analytics

We've successfully rolled out the highly requested updates to the Farmer Dashboard!

## What's New

### 👤 Unified Profile Editor
You can now securely manage all your personal and farm data directly from the newly added **Profile** page (accessible via the `Profile` icon in your dashboard dock).
- **Update Personal Details:** Update your name and phone number.
- **Manage Farm Details:** Update your Farm's name, size, and most importantly, location.

### 🌎 Dynamic Auto-Geocoding
When you enter a new address text in your profile (e.g., "Rajanukunte, Bengaluru"), our intelligent backend automatically reverse-geocodes it into precise latitude/longitude coordinates to ensure your farm is accurately tracked globally.

### 📈 Real-Time Dashboard Analytics
No more dummy data! Your Farmer Dashboard is now deeply integrated with the platform's backend services:
- **Real Revenue Trend:** The 6-month revenue chart now queries all `DELIVERED` and `COMPLETED` order items linked to your farm's products in real-time, aggregating your earnings dynamically.
- **Live NDVI Timeseries & Yield Revisions:** The historical graph now directly visualizes `NDVIReading` and `YieldPrediction` data tied to your fields from the database, reflecting real fluctuations in crop health and yield expectations over time.

## Verification
- We added the necessary API controllers to the `farm` and `auth` routers in the backend.
- We created the brand-new responsive `Profile.tsx` page.
- We updated `FarmerDashboardNew.tsx` to bind its Recharts visualizations to the backend's real responses.
- Confirmed that both the frontend and backend applications build perfectly with zero errors.

Enjoy your new real-time dashboard! 🚀

CodeContent:
# Phase 2: Yield Prediction Implementation

The ML integration for AgroTrace's Yield Prediction is now fully implemented and live on the dashboard.

## Changes Made

### 1. Synthetic Data & Model Training (`generate_synthetic_data.py`)
- We implemented a data generation script that bases its yields on real-world agronomic baselines (e.g., Rice ~4000 kg/ha, Sugarcane ~70000 kg/ha) rather than random noise.
- It applies modifiers based on `days_since_sowing`, `ndvi_trend` (simulating healthy vs stressed crops), and `cum_rainfall`/`avg_temp` (penalizing drought or extreme temperatures).
- A LightGBM Regressor was successfully trained on 5000 generated records with an RMSE of ~6946 kg (expected given the variance across crop types) and saved as `yield_model.pkl`.

### 2. ML Inference Service
- **Yield Service**: Created `yield_service.py` to lazily load the LightGBM model into memory and run fast predictions.
- **Router Integration**: Built a `POST /predict-yield` endpoint in `routers/prediction.py` and connected it to FastAPI's `main.py`.
- **Model Provenance**: The endpoint strictly checks the source of the incoming NDVI data. It correctly surfaces both `dataQuality: "SIMULATED" | "OBSERVED"` and forces `modelProvenance: "SYNTHETIC_BOOTSTRAP"`.

### 3. Backend Integration
- Updated the existing `POST /crop/:cropId` endpoint in `prediction.routes.ts`.
- The route now correctly computes `daysSinceSowing` dynamically from the crop's `plantingDate` and calculates the `ndviTrend` over the trailing 60 days.
- It calls the new `/yield/predict-yield` service using the fetched inputs and securely saves both the `aiPredictedYieldKg` back to the Crop model and the provenance flags into the `YieldPrediction` metadata.

### 4. Frontend Dashboard Updates
- Replaced the simple `BarChart` in `FarmerDashboardNew.tsx` with a powerful `ComposedChart` from Recharts.
- Conditionally renders a dashed line for simulated predictions (`dataQuality === 'SIMULATED'`) and a solid line for observed predictions.
- The custom tooltip alerts the farmer with a visible `⚠️ Preliminary Model — not yet validated against real harvests` warning badge if the model provenance is a bootstrap model.

## Validation Results
- Python dependencies successfully updated to include LightGBM, scikit-learn, and Pandas.
- LightGBM dataset generated and trained cleanly with appropriate agronomic correlation.
- The frontend visualization elegantly handles merging the AI series into the dashboard and safely handles missing data points when predictions haven't yet been run.

## Next Steps
You can test the end-to-end yield prediction by running the FastAPI ML service alongside the Node backend. If you're happy with Phase 2, we can proceed to the next phase on your command!
Description: Phase 2 walkthrough

CodeContent:
# Goal Description

The objective is to expand the "Yield Prediction by Crop" section on the Farmer Dashboard. Instead of just displaying a single graph, we will build a dedicated, comprehensive "AI Crop Intelligence" panel. This panel will display rich details about each crop's predicted yield, the underlying data quality, provenance, and actionable insights. We will also integrate a "Crop Recommendation" feature to allow farmers to get AI-driven suggestions for their next planting season.

## User Review Required
> [!IMPORTANT]
> The current dashboard fetches crops and their associated AI predictions. I propose we add a detailed **AI Crop Intelligence Table/Card Grid** alongside or directly below the chart. For each crop, it will display:
> 1. The exact AI predicted yield vs. estimated yield.
> 2. Variance percentage (e.g., +15% over expected).
> 3. The Data Quality badge (`OBSERVED` vs `SIMULATED`).
> 4. The Model Provenance warning if it's a bootstrap model.
> 
> Furthermore, I propose adding a **"Get AI Recommendation"** button for each farm field that calls our newly created Phase 3 `/recommend/field/:fieldId` endpoint and displays the top recommended crop and estimated ROI. 
> 
> Do you approve this UI approach?

## Proposed Changes

---

### Frontend Components (`apps/web/src/pages/FarmerDashboardNew.tsx`)

#### [MODIFY] [apps/web/src/pages/FarmerDashboardNew.tsx](file:///C:/Users/chinn/Desktop/AgroTrace/apps/web/src/pages/FarmerDashboardNew.tsx)
1. **Enhanced Yield Section**: 
   - Wrap the existing `ComposedChart` in a larger `AI Crop Intelligence` section.
   - Add a detailed data grid or list view below the chart. For each crop, it will break down the `estimatedYield`, `actualYield`, and `aiPredictedYieldKg`.
   - Add visual indicators (arrows up/down) for the variance between the farmer's estimate and the AI's prediction.
   - Clearly display the `dataQuality` and `modelProvenance` tags using styled badges so the farmer knows exactly how trustworthy the number is.

2. **Crop Recommendation Integration**:
   - Add a new sub-panel or modal for "Next Season Recommendations".
   - It will list the farmer's fields and provide a button to trigger the `POST /api/predict/recommend/field/:fieldId` API.
   - When triggered, it will display the `recommendedCrop`, confidence score, `expectedRoi` (with `roiBasis: "current_market_price"`), and alternative crops.

#### [MODIFY] [apps/web/src/services/api.ts or equivalent](file:///C:/Users/chinn/Desktop/AgroTrace/apps/web/src/services/api.ts) (if needed)
- Ensure the API client exposes a function to call the recommendation endpoint.

## Verification Plan

### Manual Verification
1. Open the Farmer Dashboard in the browser.
2. Verify that the new "AI Crop Intelligence" section correctly lists all crops with their detailed AI yield metrics and badges.
3. Click the "Get Recommendation" button for a field, verify the loading state, and confirm the UI accurately displays the recommended crop, ROI, and alternatives returned from the backend.

# Production-Ready Farmer Onboarding & Data Ingestion

This plan outlines the architecture to eliminate the "Default Field" workaround and introduce a true production-grade onboarding flow for fields, ensuring the ML models always have the necessary Soil and Weather data.

## User Review Required
> [!IMPORTANT]
> The current system automatically maps new crops to a "Default Field" because we lacked a UI to draw fields and input soil data. To build the production-grade flow you requested, we will need to:
> 1. Update the database schema to store Field polygons.
> 2. Add an interactive map (React-Leaflet) to the dashboard for drawing fields.
> 3. Build the background ingestion workers.
> 
> Do you approve the scope of this refactor before we proceed to the Blockchain phase, or would you prefer a simpler "Mock Data Seeder" to just unblock testing for now?

## Proposed Changes

---

### 1. Database Schema Updates

#### [MODIFY] [packages/prisma/schema.prisma](file:///C:/Users/chinn/Desktop/AgroTrace/packages/prisma/schema.prisma)
- Update `Field` model to include `polygon Json?` (GeoJSON or array of coordinates).

### 2. Frontend Map Onboarding & Soil Prompt

#### [MODIFY] [apps/web/src/pages/FarmerDashboardNew.tsx](file:///C:/Users/chinn/Desktop/AgroTrace/apps/web/src/pages/FarmerDashboardNew.tsx)
- **Field Onboarding Map**: Integrate `react-leaflet` to allow the user to drop a pin or draw a polygon when registering a new Field.
- **Missing Data Alerts**: Add a high-visibility warning at the top of the dashboard if a field is missing recent `SoilReading` or `WeatherSnapshot`.
- **Soil Entry Form**: Provide a simple modal allowing the farmer to manually input N, P, K, and pH values.

### 3. Backend Ingestion Workers & API

#### [NEW] [apps/backend/src/routes/field.routes.ts](file:///C:/Users/chinn/Desktop/AgroTrace/apps/backend/src/routes/field.routes.ts)
- Implement `POST /api/v1/fields` to save the new field and its polygon.
- Implement `POST /api/v1/fields/:id/soil` to record manual soil test results.

#### [NEW] [apps/backend/src/services/ingestion.service.ts](file:///C:/Users/chinn/Desktop/AgroTrace/apps/backend/src/services/ingestion.service.ts)
- **Automated Weather/NDVI Worker**: An asynchronous function triggered immediately after a Field is created.
  - It will extract the lat/lng from the field's polygon.
  - It will call Open-Meteo for 30-day historical weather and insert into `WeatherSnapshot`.
  - It will generate or fetch the 60-day historical NDVI sequence and insert into `NDVIReading`.

## Verification Plan

### Manual Verification
1. Log in as a brand-new Farmer.
2. Verify the "Default Field" is no longer silently created. Instead, the dashboard prompts to "Setup Your First Field".
3. Use the Map UI to create a Field.
4. Verify the backend console logs show the automated Weather and NDVI ingestion running in the background.
5. Verify the dashboard immediately prompts for Soil Data.
6. Enter Soil Data, and confirm the AI Yield Prediction and Recommendation endpoints now work perfectly without any 400 errors.

CodeContent:
# Debugging AI Crop Yield Prediction Pipeline

This document details the root cause analysis and the proposed fixes for the logical inconsistencies found in the AI yield prediction pipeline.

## 1. Root Cause Analysis & Findings

### Area Unit Mismatch
- **Source**: `apps/web/src/pages/Crops.tsx` (Line 228) asks the user for "Area (Acres)".
- **Issue**: The backend controller (`crop.controller.ts`) saves this value directly into the database. While `schema.prisma` comments state the field is `// in hectares`, it is actually storing Acres. 
- **Impact**: In `prediction.routes.ts`, the backend passes `crop.area` directly to the AI service as `areaHectares`. A 1 Acre crop is treated as a 1 Hectare crop, which is a massive 2.47x overestimation of the physical land size, leading to highly inflated yield predictions.

### Days Sown Calculation
- **Source**: `apps/backend/src/routes/prediction.routes.ts` (Line 61)
- **Calculation**: `Math.floor((new Date().getTime() - plantingDate.getTime()) / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24))`
- **Result**: A crop planted on 30-07-2026 evaluated on 31-07-2026 correctly results in `days_sown = 1`. The calculation is mathematically correct. The issue is that a 1-day old crop is being paired with an unrealistic NDVI score.

### NDVI Source
- **Source**: `apps/backend/src/routes/prediction.routes.ts` (Lines 41-50)
- **Issue**: The query fetches the last 60 days of NDVI readings for the *Field*, not the *Crop*. Because the crop was just planted 1 day ago, the query is picking up the high NDVI readings (0.663) from the *previous* mature crop grown on that same field!
- **Impact**: The model thinks a 1-day old seedling has a dense, lush green canopy (NDVI 0.663), drastically confusing the LightGBM Regressor. 

### Prediction Route Trace
1. **Frontend**: `Crops.tsx` → User enters area in Acres.
2. **Database**: `crop.controller.ts` → Saved as raw float (Acres).
3. **Trigger**: `FarmerDashboardNew.tsx` → Calls `/crop/:cropId`
4. **API Endpoint**: `prediction.routes.ts` → Grabs old field NDVI, passes Acres as Hectares.
5. **Feature Engineering**: AI service receives faulty Hectares and faulty NDVI.
6. **Model**: `yield_service.py` LightGBM predicts inflated yield.

---

## 2. Proposed Changes

### `apps/backend/src/routes/prediction.routes.ts`
- **[MODIFY]**: Convert `crop.area` (Acres) to `areaHectares` by multiplying by `0.404686`.
- **[MODIFY]**: Update the NDVI query. Instead of a hardcoded 60 days, filter readings by `capturedAt: { gte: crop.plantingDate }`.
- **[MODIFY]**: If no NDVI readings exist since planting (which is common for a 1-day old crop), default to a realistic bare-soil/seedling NDVI baseline (e.g., `0.15`) instead of `0.5`.
- **[MODIFY]**: Add `console.log` for the `inputSnapshot` to fulfill the requirement of logging the exact payload leaving the Node backend.

### `apps/ml-inference/services/yield_service.py`
- **[MODIFY]**: Implement Python `logging` to print the exact dataframe, feature names, and `dtypes` immediately before calling `model.predict()`.
- **[MODIFY]**: Add logical validation checks before prediction.
  ```python
  if area_unit == "acre":
      logger.info("Converting acres to hectares") # Note: We will do this on the Node side, but we will add loggers.
  
  if days_since_sowing < 5 and ndvi_trend > 0.3:
      logger.warning(f"Validation Warning: NDVI {ndvi_trend} is unrealistically high for a {days_since_sowing}-day old crop.")
  ```

---

## 3. User Review Required

> [!WARNING]
> Because the database currently stores Acres but the schema expected Hectares, I am proposing that we fix the conversion at the Prediction Route boundary (converting the Acres stored in the DB to Hectares before sending to the AI). 
> 
> Alternatively, we could change the UI to ask for Hectares, or change the Backend `createCrop` to convert to Hectares on save. Please confirm if handling the conversion in the Prediction route is acceptable for your evaluation.

## 4. Verification Plan
- Create a new test crop with 1 Acre.
- Run the prediction.
- Verify the Node terminal logs the Acre->Hectare conversion.
- Verify the Python AI terminal logs the warning for the NDVI (if simulated) and logs the full feature dataframe schema.
- Confirm the yield prediction drops to a mathematically sound level.

ArtifactMetadata.Summary: Walkthrough of the fixes implemented for the prediction pipeline.

CodeContent:
# Prediction Pipeline Debugging & Validation Completed

I have fully implemented the architectural improvements and validation layers across the AI Yield Prediction pipeline to ensure perfect alignment with real-world farming logic and data integrity.

## 1. Area Unit Handling
- **Database Migration**: A script was executed that successfully converted all existing crops in the database (10 crops) from raw Acres to true Hectares by multiplying by `0.404686`.
- **Backend API (`crop.controller.ts`)**: When a user creates or edits a crop, the area passed (in Acres) is instantly converted into Hectares before persisting to Prisma.
- **Frontend UI (`Crops.tsx` & `FarmerDashboardNew.tsx`)**: The UI fetches the stored Hectares and safely divides by `0.404686`, formatting to 2 decimal places to seamlessly display Acres back to the user without data corruption.

## 2. NDVI Temporal Filtering
- **Backend API (`prediction.routes.ts`)**: The NDVI lookup query is now strictly constrained to `capturedAt: { gte: plantingDate }`. 
- **Baseline Defaulting**: If a crop was planted today and has 0 remote sensing readings, the prediction route correctly fails over to a bare-soil/seedling baseline NDVI of `0.15` instead of bleeding over mature `0.663` readings from the previous season.

## 3. Strict Input Validation
- **Harvest Dates (`crop.controller.ts`)**: Creating or updating a crop will now throw a `400 Bad Request` if the expected harvest date is before the planting date, or if it implies an unrealistic growing cycle of less than 20 days.
- **Model Validation (`yield_service.py`)**: Python loggers will now emit `WARNING` flags in the terminal before prediction if variables are out of biological bounds (e.g., negative rainfall, extreme temps, or high NDVI for a young crop).

## 4. Advanced Trace Logging
- **Model Tracing (`yield_service.py`)**: The `input_df` is printed in full, along with `input_df.dtypes`, ensuring every feature, unit, and data type sent to LightGBM is entirely visible in the Python terminal for judging and auditing.

## Next Steps
To test these changes:
1. Make sure to **restart the `AgroTrace - AI Service` terminal** (if it's not running with `--reload`) so that it picks up the Python validation updates.
2. Go to the dashboard and try to edit a crop's harvest date to be *before* its planting date (it will be blocked!).
3. Create a brand new 1-Acre crop for today and hit "Run AI".
4. Check the Python terminal to see the `0.15` NDVI baseline being used and the full DataFrame feature log being generated!

CodeContent:
# Consumer-to-Farmer Marketplace with Distributor Commission

This plan implements the complete end-to-end flow where consumers book crops from farmers, pay a price inclusive of a distributor commission, and the farmer physically dispatches the order to the distributor for supply chain routing.

## User Review Required
> [!IMPORTANT]
> - **Commission Rate**: I am proposing a **5%** standard distributor commission fee on top of the farmer's base price. Is 5% acceptable, or would you prefer a different rate?
> - **Status Flow**: The flow will be: `Consumer Orders` -> Shipment is `PENDING_FARMER` -> `Farmer Clicks "Dispatch"` -> Shipment becomes `ASSIGNED` -> `Distributor Claims it` -> Supply chain continues as normal.

## Proposed Changes

### Backend API Updates

#### [MODIFY] [order.controller.ts](file:///C:/Users/chinn/Desktop/AgroTrace/apps/backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts)
- **Fix Pricing Calculation**: Update `createOrder` to calculate order item prices as `product.price * 1.05` (farmer price + 5% distributor commission), rather than the arbitrary current calculation.
- **Initial Shipment Status**: When creating a new order, initialize its associated `Shipment` record with status `PENDING_FARMER` (instead of `ASSIGNED`) so that it doesn't immediately appear in the distributor queue until the farmer dispatches it.

#### [MODIFY] [shipment.controller.ts](file:///C:/Users/chinn/Desktop/AgroTrace/apps/backend/src/controllers/shipment.controller.ts)
- **Update Shipment Logic**: Modify `updateShipmentStatus` to allow farmers to update a shipment from `PENDING_FARMER` to `ASSIGNED` (indicating it has been dispatched and is ready for a distributor to claim).

---

### Frontend Updates

#### [MODIFY] [Marketplace.tsx](file:///C:/Users/chinn/Desktop/AgroTrace/apps/web/src/pages/Marketplace.tsx)
- **UI Pricing**: Display all product prices as `base_price * 1.05` to match the backend.
- **Transparency Tag**: Add a visible badge or text below the price stating `(Includes 5% distributor fee)` so the consumer understands the pricing breakdown.

#### [MODIFY] [FarmerDashboardNew.tsx](file:///C:/Users/chinn/Desktop/AgroTrace/apps/web/src/pages/FarmerDashboardNew.tsx)
- **Orders Management**: Add a new "Orders" tab/panel in the Farmer dashboard.
- **Dispatch Action**: Fetch orders using `orderService.getFarmerOrders()`. Display them to the farmer with a "Dispatch to Distributor" button for orders that are pending fulfillment. This button will update the shipment status to `ASSIGNED`.

## Verification Plan
1. Create a product as a Farmer.
2. Log in as a Consumer, verify the marketplace shows the price + 5% commission, and place an order.
3. Log in as a Farmer, navigate to the Orders panel, and click "Dispatch to Distributor".
4. Log in as a Distributor, go to the Transport dashboard, and claim the newly dispatched shipment.

ArtifactMetadata.Summary: Implementation plan for adding Marketplace Listing capability to Farmer Dashboard

CodeContent:
# Enable Farmers to List Crops on the Marketplace

Provide a brief description of the problem, any background context, and what the change accomplishes.
Currently, AgroTrace tracks your agricultural items in two different stages:
1. **Crops**: These are the physical plants growing on your farm (tracked for NDVI, growth stages, AI yield prediction).
2. **Products**: These are the packaged, harvested items explicitly listed for sale on the consumer Marketplace.

The reason you are only seeing dummy crops as a consumer is because there is currently **no button in the Farmer Dashboard to convert a harvested "Crop" into a "Product"** that is available for sale. The backend API supports it, but the UI was never built!

This plan will build the missing UI so you can actually list your crops.

## Proposed Changes

### [MODIFY] [productService.ts](file:///C:/Users/chinn/Desktop/AgroTrace/apps/web/src/services/productService.ts)
- Update the `createProduct` function signature to include the `price` field, ensuring farmers can set a price when listing their product.

### [MODIFY] [FarmerDashboardNew.tsx](file:///C:/Users/chinn/Desktop/AgroTrace/apps/web/src/pages/FarmerDashboardNew.tsx)
- Add a **"List on Marketplace"** button to the crop cards (or for crops that are ready to harvest).
- Create a new **Product Listing Modal** that will prompt the farmer for:
  - Product Name (e.g., "Premium Organic Wheat")
  - Price per kg
  - Quantity available to sell
  - Batch Number
- When submitted, this will call `productService.createProduct()`, generating the blockchain QR code and instantly making it visible on the Consumer Marketplace.

## Verification Plan
1. Log in as a Farmer.
2. Click the new "List on Marketplace" button on one of the existing crops.
3. Fill out the pricing and batch details.
4. Log out and log back in as a Consumer.
5. Verify that the newly created product appears in the Marketplace and can be added to the cart!

ArtifactMetadata.Summary: Standardize entire application on Hectares

CodeContent:
# Standardization on Hectares

Currently, the application attempts to let the user work in Acres on the frontend while saving as Hectares in the database. As you noticed, this introduces a messy split in logic. 

Since the core AI Yield Prediction model (`LightGBM Regressor`) was trained specifically on **Hectares**, the most robust solution is to standardize the *entire* application—both frontend UI and backend database—strictly on **Hectares**.

## Proposed Changes

### [MODIFY] [Farms.tsx](file:///C:/Users/chinn/Desktop/AgroTrace/apps/web/src/pages/Farms.tsx)
- Change all UI labels from "Acres" to "Hectares" when registering a farm.
- Remove the temporary `0.404686` display conversion introduced in the previous step.

### [MODIFY] [Crops.tsx](file:///C:/Users/chinn/Desktop/AgroTrace/apps/web/src/pages/Crops.tsx)
- Change the area input field label from "Acres" to "Hectares".

### [MODIFY] [FarmerDashboardNew.tsx](file:///C:/Users/chinn/Desktop/AgroTrace/apps/web/src/pages/FarmerDashboardNew.tsx)
- Update the Crop Cards to display the area simply as `X Hectares` (removing the mathematical conversion).

### [MODIFY] [farm.controller.ts](file:///C:/Users/chinn/Desktop/AgroTrace/apps/backend/src/controllers/farm.controller.ts)
- Remove the `* 0.404686` conversion logic when creating and updating farms, because the frontend will now send Hectares natively.

### [MODIFY] [crop.controller.ts](file:///C:/Users/chinn/Desktop/AgroTrace/apps/backend/src/controllers/crop.controller.ts)
- Remove the `* 0.404686` conversion logic when creating and updating crops.
- Update error messages to refer to "Hectares" instead of "Acres".

## Database Status
The database is already perfectly prepared for this change! The migration script we just ran successfully standardized all existing data to Hectares. 

## User Review Required
> [!IMPORTANT]
> Is standardizing exclusively on **Hectares** acceptable? (This is highly recommended since the AI model expects hectares). If you strongly prefer Acres, I will have to edit the AI model pipeline to convert Acres to Hectares right before inference.
Description: Implementation plan to standardize the app on Hectares.
